Definition: from G3844 and G3089; to loosen beside, i.e. relax (perfect passive participle, paralyzed or enfeebled):--feeble, sick of the (taken with) palsy.
BiblicalUsage: Paralyō means to loosen, to relax, to be palsied, enfeebled. Men bring one taken with a palsy, lying on a bed; Peter finds Aeneas, who has kept his bed eight years and is sick of the palsy; and Hebrews says, Lift up the hands which hang down, and the feeble knees.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the palsied and the feeble are the same call: lift up what hangs down, and let the Healer straighten what is loose.
